''Erythrina fulgens'' Lois. |synonyms_ref = {{cite web|url = http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl/record/ild-12306|title = Erythrina americana Mill. — The Plant List|publisher = [[The Plant List]]|website = theplantlist.org|accessdate = 4 September 2016}} }} '''''Erythrina americana''''' ('''coral tree''', '''colorines''', '''colorín''', or '''pemoches'''), is a flowering plant of the genus ''[[Erythrina]]'' which is native to Mexico. Colorín (plural colorines) is the name of a type of tree, ''Erythrina americana'' also called '''Tzompāmitl'''. The word colorín means color chillón—a “gaudy” or “loud” color (Williams 1959). Colorines plant also called, cuchillitos (little knives) or machetitos (little [[machete]]s), zompantle, or coral is a nice flower, red in color and every individual flower resembles a little machete, the flower is edible{{cite web|url=http://vivedeviaje.com.mx/2010/10/cocinando-flores-de-colorin-carlos-lazaro/|title=Cocinando Flores de Colorín – Carlos Lázaro|website=vivedeviaje.com.mx|accessdate=4 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160918110657/http://vivedeviaje.com.mx/2010/10/cocinando-flores-de-colorin-carlos-lazaro/#|archive-date=2016-09-18|url-status=dead}} and is boiled (only the red part of the flower) and cooked with scrambled eggs or tuna in many parts of south Mexico. [[File:Colorines plant from the Texan Desert.jpg|thumb|Colorines, machetitos machete Erythrina americana plant from Texas]] This variety flowers during the dry season (April) in many parts, and the plant is very popular with hummingbirds because of the bright red color, the plant ranges from a few feet off the ground to trees five meters tall. The earliest depiction of this tree in America is in the [[Florentine Codex]]. In the 17th century, Francisco Hernández commented: "The juice from the flowers of this tree, given to children induces drowsiness and sleepless".{{cite web|url=https://www.tlahui.com/medic/medic20/colorin.htm|title=Zompantle o colorín (Erythrina americana Miller). Tlahui - Medic No. 20, II/2005|publisher=|website=tlahui.edu.mx|accessdate=4 September 2016}} Other sites explain that although the flower is edible,{{Cite web |url=http://www.jornadamorelos.com/2013/1/12/cultura_nota_02.php# |title=La Jornada Morelos en Internet |access-date=2014-04-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407083222/http://www.jornadamorelos.com/2013/1/12/cultura_nota_02.php# |archive-date=2014-04-07 |url-status=dead }} the seeds and everything else in the tree is highly toxic, in Mexico, the pulverized seeds are used as rat poison and the bark is used as fish poison.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pnnHgcasN-cC|title=Edible and Useful Plants of Texas and the Southwest: A Practical Guide|first=Delena|last=Tull|date=1 January 1999|publisher=[[University of Texas Press]]|isbn=9780292781641 |accessdate=4 September 2016|via=[[Google Books]]}} ==Description== ''E. americana'' is a tree that grows to 4-5m. It has pale, brown, smooth bark and a spreading and profusely branching [[Crown (botany)|crown]]. It sheds its leaves during winter and the dry season. Leaves are . It has [[Thorns, spines, and prickles#Spines|sprines]] on the branches and conical, flat spines on the trunk. Leaves are arranged [[Leaf#Arrangement_on_the_stem|alternately]] and are [[Glossary of leaf morphology#Leaf structure|trifoliate]] with [[Glossary of leaf morphology#Leaf and leaflet shapes|rhombic-ovate]] leaflets that are 7-22cm long and broad.{{r|eb2001}} ==Uses== The flower is edible, This tree is very popular with kids who use the flowers as a little knives to stab each other. The ground seeds and bark are used as poison, The tree is also used to make traditional crafts in many Mexican states, specially traditional dance masks{{dead link|date=September 2016}} and is also used as fence post in many parts of Veracruz Mexico, it is a beautiful and hardy tree, some varieties even tolerate frost. The tall varieties of this plant are rarely used as a garden plant, but the dwarf varieties are used as garden plants because they tolerate frost, they tolerate heat and come from dry places, and they flower early and attract hummingbirds.
